newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBJ says to raise May long-term prime to 3.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: IBJ says to raise May long-term prime to 3.1 pct.

text.p: The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) said on Monday it would raise its long-term prime lending rate for May to 3.1 percent, effective from May 14, from 2.5 percent in April.
The new rate will be the highest since August 1996, when it was 3.3 percent.
The IBJ also said it would raise the coupon rate of its May five-year debenture to be sold to institutional investors by 0.6 point to 2.2 percent from 1.6 percent for the April issue.
The prime rate, which is applied to loans of one year and longer to Japanese long-term credit banks' most creditworthy clients, is reviewed every month, reflecting market trends.
The prime rate, which is also a key reference rate for other banks making long-term loans, was cut by 0.2 point to a record low 2.5 percent in December and had remained unchanged since then.

The IBJ customarily sets its prime rate 0.9 percentage point above the coupon rate of its five-year debenture, which is issued monthly and is the benchmark in Japan's debenture market. Bank debentures are the long-term credit banks' major fund-raising tool.
IBJ's April 1.6 percent five-year debenture was offer-only at 2.26 percent on Monday afternoon after trading at 2.30 percent on Friday.

The other two long-term credit banks, the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd, are to announce their new prime rates and terms for May debentures on Tuesday. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
